cards.explanation: The answer is many loans. The taunt says, "Woe to him who amasses what is not his and makes himself rich with many loans!" (Habakkuk 2:6). He's stacking up debts like I stack cooling racks, friends, and nobody stacks that high without a wobble.

The answer is False. The verse asks, "Will not your creditors suddenly arise and those who disturb you awaken? Then you will become their prey." (Habakkuk 2:7). Those who are owed wake up and rise suddenly. He becomes their prey, and the verse says nothing about them forgetting.

The answer is because he plundered many nations. God says, "Because you have plundered many nations, the remnant of the people will plunder you…" (Habakkuk 2:8). What he did to them comes back around to him, friends. That's a boomerang with a very long throw.
The word is unjust. "Woe to him who builds his house by unjust gain…" (Habakkuk 2:9). Notice the woe isn't aimed at the house itself, bakers. It's aimed at the unjust gain the house was built with.

The answer is the hand of disaster. He builds his house high "…to place his nest on high and escape the hand of disaster!" (Habakkuk 2:9). I think he figured the higher the nest, the safer the guy. Climbing up is a lot of work for a plan like that, friends.

The answer is stones! "For the stones will cry out from the wall, and the rafters will echo it from the woodwork." (Habakkuk 2:11). The walls he built are the ones that speak up, and then the rafters echo it from the woodwork. Picture building a house and then the bricks start talking, bakers.

The answer is True. God says, "Woe to him who builds a city with bloodshed and establishes a town by iniquity!" (Habakkuk 2:12). That's woe number three in this passage, friends. The woe before it was about a house in verse 9, and this one is about a whole city built with bloodshed.

The answer is the knowledge of the LORD's glory. "For the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the LORD as the waters cover the sea." (Habakkuk 2:14). After all those woes, friends, this verse hits like the oven door opening on a fresh batch. The earth gets filled with the knowledge of His glory.
The answer is shame. God says, "You will be filled with shame instead of glory." (Habakkuk 2:16). Shame takes the spot where glory was, bakers. That's a swap nobody would sign up for.

The word is LORD's. "The cup in the LORD’s right hand will come around to you…" (Habakkuk 2:16). He was pouring drinks for his neighbors, friends, and now a cup is coming around to him. It's the LORD's right hand that holds it.

The answer is Lebanon. God says, "For your violence against Lebanon will overwhelm you…" (Habakkuk 2:17). The violence against Lebanon is what overwhelms him, friends. That's the place the verse names.
The answer is True. God says, "…the destruction of animals will terrify you…" (Habakkuk 2:17). Terror is what comes to the proud man. This part is heavy, friends, so I'll keep the jokes in the oven.

The answer is idols that cannot speak. "For its maker trusts in his own creation; he makes idols that cannot speak." (Habakkuk 2:18). The maker trusts what he made, bakers, and what he made can't say a single word back. The verse even calls the idol a teacher of lies.

The answer is False. The verse says, "Behold, it is overlaid with gold and silver, yet there is no breath in it at all." (Habakkuk 2:19). Sprinkles on a cookie don't make it breathe, friends, and gold doesn't either. The gold and silver cover the outside, and there's still no breath in it.

The answer is in His holy temple. "But the LORD is in His holy temple…" (Habakkuk 2:20). After all that talk of silent idols, bakers, this is the one who is there. The idols have gold on them and no breath in them. Then comes the call: "let all the earth be silent before Him."

The answer is be silent. "let all the earth be silent before Him." (Habakkuk 2:20). I'll be honest, friends, silence is hard for a guy with a mustache this talkative, but I'm working on it. All the earth is asked to be quiet, not just me.
